nearest_terminal_family_challenges.reason: The terminal factor compares adjacent closes and has 238 within-half transitions. Campaign106 never reads close or adjacency: a bar can have high>low while its close is unchanged, and closes can change between two high=low bars.

Campaign105 observes positive volume/amount clock occupancy and reads no price. Campaign106 observes within-minute high-low variation and reads no activity; active one-price bars and inactive source states separate the mechanisms.

The entropy factor normalizes positive log-range magnitudes and used a 120-positive-range support gate. Campaign106 discards every positive magnitude, uses a fixed denominator 240, retains any zero-to-240 varying-bar count, and has no positive-total or support minimum.

nearest_terminal_family_challenges.family: range clock center variance profile similarity and local-peak families
nearest_terminal_family_challenges.reason: Those factors retain range magnitude and/or clock order. Campaign106 is invariant to both once the binary zero-versus-positive mask count is fixed.

nearest_terminal_family_challenges.family: intrabar body wick close-location and unchanged-close range-absorption families
nearest_terminal_family_challenges.reason: Those mechanisms require open and/or close or partition range mass by candle state. Campaign106 reads only high and low and does not condition on another state.

nearest_terminal_family_challenges.family: Candidate49 intraday cumulative VWAP crossing rate
nearest_terminal_family_challenges.reason: Candidate49 combines cumulative amount/volume transaction price with close and remains prospective-only. Campaign106 uses no close, amount, volume, cumulative path, or crossing.
